messages.content:
Diagnosis:

The bug is related to selection of namespaced attributes using a wildcard "@" in XPath expressions. According to the current bug report, when selecting attributes with a wildcard like xml/@*, namespaced attributes are not returned (selectSingleNode returns null), but explicitly selecting with a namespace prefix like @x:* works fine.

The code snippet from the method DOMAttributeIterator.testAttr(Attr attr) shows the logic that tests whether an attribute matches the requested QName name:

- It first extracts the nodePrefix and nodeLocalName from the attribute.
- It skips attributes with prefix "xmlns" or localName "xmlns".
- It compares the local name of the attribute against the QName name's local name, allowing either a wildcard "*" or exact match.
- It then gets the testPrefix from the QName.
- The crucial condition is at line 84:
  if (equalStrings(testPrefix, nodePrefix)) return true;
- Otherwise, it compares namespace URIs of the testPrefix and nodePrefix to decide if it matches.

The bug report suggests this condition is problematic when the testPrefix is null (e.g., using "@*" without any prefix). In that case, it will only return true if nodePrefix is also null. But if the attribute has a prefix (namespaced), the testPrefix is null and the condition will fail, so the namespaced attribute will not be selected.

The probable fix is to change the condition from 
`if (equalStrings(testPrefix, nodePrefix)) return true;` 
to 
`if (testPrefix==null || equalStrings(testPrefix, nodePrefix)) return true;`
so that if the testPrefix is null (wildcard for prefix), it matches any nodePrefix (including non-null ones), thus including namespaced attributes.

This matches exactly the scenario reported: wildcard @* should select all attributes regardless of prefix, and currently it does not select namespaced attributes because testPrefix is null but nodePrefix is not, so the method returns false.

Therefore, the root cause is the strict prefix equality check in testAttr that does not handle null testPrefix properly when selecting attributes with XPath wildcard for attributes.

The fix should be applied in DOMAttributeIterator.testAttr(Attr) method.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
